messages:
Sam: Post-mortem highlight: during the last active/active swap the tenants residency flag plus a pending legal consent caused oscillation. Idea: introduce an evacuation-quorum layer that treats consent services as voters with weights. If quorum reached -> safe failover, else use degraded mode. Thoughts?

Priya: Interesting. Quorum gives us clearer rules vs ad-hoc latches. But voters (legal, escrow, tenant) have different trust levels and latency. We need weighted timeouts and a fallback policy when quorum stalls.

Lucas: Implementation sketch: control-plane collects votes from sources: escrow-service, tenant-policy-store, and manual-operator. Each vote: {source,id,weight,ts,state}. Quorum formula: sum(weights where state=ok) >= threshold. Default threshold 0.7 of total weight. If quorum not met in T_quorum -> invoke degraded path (serve-local-anonymized or redirect).

Mei: Two engineering concerns: 1) voters must be highly available and have bounded latency; 2) we must avoid blocking data-plane on quorum checks for every write. Cache quorum decision per-tenant for short TTL and use dataplane header X-Evac-Quorum: <decision_id>.

Priya: Also need safety override: if infra health indicates region unrecoverable, override quorum after emergency_deadline but log and notify legal. Availability must win in critical cases.

Sam: UX: Console should show current voter states and a live quorum score to help operators during cutovers. Audit trail required.

Lucas: Storage: votes are small records in control-plane store, append-only events for audit. Decision state exported to telemetry and allowed to be consumed by dataplane via short-lived tokens.

Mei: Performance: measure latency p95 for vote collection. If >50ms it will harm tail latency. Plan B: optimistic local decision + async reconciliation (with stronger guarantees for metadata writes).

legal: Quick note: legal votes are specialthey may impose non-failable constraints in some jurisdictions. We need a voter type that can veto instead of weight. Config must allow marking sources as veto-capable.

Sam: Agreed. So we support weighted voters + explicit veto flags. Default: escrow=weight 0.4, tenant-policy=0.3, operator=0.2, legal=veto. Threshold 0.7.

Priya: Rollout plan: feature-flag, start with non-PII tenants, add UI for voter visibility, run chaos tests that inject slow or failing voters.

Lucas: Dataplane contract: X-Evac-Quorum-Decision: <id>, X-Evac-Mode: quorum|degraded|override. Dataplane uses cached decision until TTL expiry then fetch fresh.

Mei: Action items:
- Lucas: proto for voter collector + quorum eval (due Wed)
- Priya: console wireframes + alert rules (due Fri)
- Sam: legal sync about veto semantics (schedule)

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: evac-quorum-canary-2024-06-15 at 2024-06-15T03:00Z. Results will be posted.

Sam: Quick poll: thumbs-up on quorum model? react with :thumbsup: or :thumbsdown:.

Priya: :thumbsup:
Lucas: :thumbsup:
Mei: :thumbsup:
legal: :neutral_face: (needs guarantees doc)

Sam: Noted. We'll add a guarantees section in the RFC. Closing thread for now. If blockers ping me.
